finding: March 2026 full-size pickup mean transaction price was $65,964; February was $66,141. Luxury full-size pickups are a separate category. The table excludes applied consumer incentives.
methodology: This is a mean, not a median, MSRP or out-the-door quote. The March report was in an April 2026 release file and contemporaneous coverage, before upload; its exact release day was not recovered. A full-year 2026 average was not yet observable.

finding: U.S. 2024 pretax household money-income median was $83,730. Table A-2 reports 10.1% at $150K–$199,999 and 16.0% at $200K or more, totaling 26.1% at $150K or more.
methodology: Calendar 2024 income collected in the 2025 CPS ASEC; U.S. households, not individuals or truck purchasers. Money income is pretax and is not take-home pay. No 2026 income estimate is inferred.

finding: In Q4 2025, 20.3% of financed new purchases had monthly payments of at least $1,000. Mean term was 69.6 months and APR 6.7%.
methodology: The relevant denominator is financed new purchases in the transaction sample. Cash purchases and leases cannot silently enter it; dollar thresholds include exactly $1,000.

finding: In Q1 2026, 43% of new loans involving negative-equity trade-ins extended to 84 months. All-new-vehicle mean term was 70.3 months and APR 6.9%.
methodology: This covers new vehicles with negative-equity trade-ins, not trucks alone. Direct Python retrieval returned HTTP403; the original page was accessible through web extraction/search. Different samples and quarters must not be merged.

finding: Nearly 30% of new financed vehicles had 73–84-month terms in Q4 2025. The mean new rate was 6.37%, versus 11.26% for used vehicles.
methodology: Original institutional release dated March 5, 2026. All-new financing term shares are not truck-specific; rate differences from Edmunds are not automatically errors.

finding: Purchase affordability requires considering financing, insurance, fuel, maintenance and other ownership costs alongside the household budget.
methodology: Pre-upload review date displayed, but no upload-day HTML capture. This guidance gives no universal salary or 20/4/10 requirement.

finding: Compare APR, interest rate, term, amount financed and total cost rather than the payment alone.
methodology: Pre-upload review date displayed. APR can include credit costs beyond note interest; a fee-free monthly model does not certify an actual lender offer.

finding: Depreciation and loan amortization jointly determine vehicle equity; rolling negative equity into a replacement loan raises its principal.
methodology: Original June 2024 PDF search extraction reviewed. This does not verify a universal instantaneous 20% truck loss or a particular residual value.

finding: For selected 2025 half-ton crew-cab models, modeled cost was $14,781 annually at 15K miles, including depreciation and finance charges. Insurance was $1,699 annually, license/registration/taxes $1,098, and maintenance/repair/tires 11.36 cents per mile.
methodology: Five selected top-selling models per category and a five-year cost framework; this is not a quote for one $50K truck or a seven-year cash budget. Loan principal is not an additional expense alongside depreciation. September 2026 findings were not used.

finding: Current 2026 XLT starting MSRP is $44,695 before $2,795 destination and other fees. The model adds to the base model and offers multiple cab, engine and bed configurations.
methodology: Current page, not an archived May quote. Current builder lists XL below XLT; Ford pages differ on the XL starting configuration. Do not use current prices to declare an exact historical MSRP false.

finding: Current manufacturer 2026 page lists WT at $37,200 and LT at $48,200 starting. LT is not the lowest WT trim.
methodology: Main URL now defaults to 2027; the explicit previous-year link was followed. Search index showed $47,900 while live page showed $48,200. Exact May price, destination basis and configuration remain unverified.

finding: The original manufacturer fleet guide distinguishes Tradesman and Big Horn and lists different equipment groups. It does not independently certify the transcript’s exact historical $47,500 configuration.
methodology: Original manufacturer search extraction and current Ram page reviewed. Exact issue date and historical price basis remain unverified; no equal towing or payload capacity is inferred.

finding: NVES studies new U.S. car and light-truck owners. The claimed original truck-usage tables and 250K truck-specific sample were not recovered.
methodology: Current institutional context only. Field dates, weighting, questions and the quoted 75/70/35/90 and 63/32/87 percentages remain unavailable. F-150 owners cannot stand for all truck owners.

finding: Q1 2026 median usual weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers were $1,235 before taxes and other deductions.
methodology: Age16+ full-time wage/salary workers in the CPS; individual gross earnings are not household income or measured median take-home pay. Taxes and deductions are missing.

finding: Stocks fluctuate and losses are possible. A future 8% return is not guaranteed.
methodology: Current investor guidance with no recovered historical publication date. It does not establish a historical S&P500 average or a retirement outcome.

finding: The index publisher distinguishes price, net total and total returns across different annualized windows. Its current snapshot does not verify the video’s undefined historical 8% average.
methodology: Later/current index snapshot is explicitly retrospective. No post-upload market return is used as evidence the creator could have known it. Period, dividends, fees and return convention remain essential.
